genre_note: Cluster c30 is two genres wearing one label. Nine documents are reported technology journalism (Epic v. Google, US v. Google, the Masimo/Apple Watch import ban, FTX, COP28, EV politics, Cybertruck safety, video games in 2023, the fediverse essay) plus three long-form reviews (Echo Frames, K.O. II, Castlevania: Nocturne). Eight are commerce documents — four deal roundups, two gift guides, one shipping-deadline table, one Prime Day FAQ — and they carry roughly half the cluster's 50,752 words while making almost no claims. The building-block distribution follows: empirical_observation dominates (dated events, testimony, price and spec listings), concept is second (entities, programs, protocols, product features), argument and counter_argument appear only where a document actually argues — the fediverse essay, the Sweeney interview, the Apple Watch legal analysis, the Cybertruck piece, and the review verdicts, where a rebuttal is a genuine speech act rather than a label. model is rare and reserved for real mechanisms: the ActivityPub data model, the Craigslist-unbundling analogy, and Google's crawl-index-rank pipeline. procedure appears six times only where the source gives ordered steps (K.O. II sampling and punch-in workflow, Echo Frames controls, the two-part burden of proving intent in the FTX case). NO hypothesis note is produced and no navigation note is produced: nothing in these twenty documents states a testable prediction as a hypothesis — the closest, the fediverse essay's closing forecast, is argued for rather than proposed, so it is filed as argument. That absence is the finding, not a gap. On decomposition: the roundups were split by topical section (brand, product category, retailer, carrier), never by word count, because a merged "deals" note would be retrieved for everything and answer nothing. Where the same product is deal-listed in several documents — WIRED's Prime Day general and Apple roundups share verbatim blocks, and the Verge headphone roundup, the WIRED pre-Black-Friday post, and the kids gift guide overlap with them — one shared note takes blocks from every document rather than near-duplicate notes splitting the evidence; 21 such cross-roundup notes sit in two dedicated sub-plans. The same rule produced two cross-document notes in the news half: the Microsoft/Activision Blizzard King acquisition (doc_0050 plus Sweeney's EU-testimony aside in doc_0170) and Epic's 2023 layoffs and overspending (Sweeney's own account in doc_0170 plus the layoff tally in doc_0050), and one shared argument note where doc_0032 and doc_0014 make the identical "switching search defaults is easy" defense. Drops are section headers, image credits, "read our guide" links, affiliate disclosures, newsletter plugs, and pull quotes that duplicate body text verbatim. Two drop-candidates were assigned instead because they contradict their own articles: the Verge editor's note at doc_0170[71] correcting Sweeney's false claim that Fortnite outdraws all of Steam, and the caption at doc_0241[34] establishing that the Apple Watch SE is exempt from the very ban the headline announces. Estimated assignment is above 94% of words for every document; the lowest are the WIRED Apple roundup (~92%, dense with per-section "read our guide" pointers) and doc_0527 (~85%, whose 981 words include a magazine subscription pitch and an affiliate disclosure).
